A hollow in an old cactus, just beyond the stream. It is dry and warm, and I have a roost in it all winter. I keep the eggs and young there. The stream is not my home. I hunt by the stream, but it is not my home.

A hollow in an old cactus. A short stem, dry and rough, with a wide hole. I have roosted in it since I was a nestling. I can hear the wind stirring the leaves and the rain dripping from the leaves. My home is the hollow in the old cactus. It is dry and warm. I have a mate and two owlets in the nest. The hollow is where I roost and sleep. I can hear the stream from there. I can hear the road. I can hear the meadow. I can hear the forest. I can hear the night. I can hear the silence. I can hear my name.

I have a hollow in the old cactus at the edge of the wood. It is dry and warm and I have lined it with leaves and feathers. I sit in it when it rains and when I am tired. I have a separate den in the ivy by the stream, where I go when I am brooding. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I have a hollow in the old cactus by the stream. It is deep, dry, and warm. I have scratched it out with my beak and claws. The stream is below, the meadow beyond, and the barn with lights is far away. I am safe here.

My home is the hollow in the old cactus. It is deep, and I have a soft place where I roost. I can feel the wood through my feathers. I have a mate and two young. They are in the hollow too. The hollow is dark and warm. I can hear the wind through the leaves. I am safe here.
A hollow in the old cactus, with a narrow opening in the bark. I have roosted there since I was a baby. The wind comes through the opening and I shiver. I keep a dry place inside for the eggs.

My home is the hollow in the old cactus at the edge of the wood. It is dark, deep, and warm. I have made a nest of leaves and feathers. The entrance is just wide enough for me to squeeze in. A hollow in an old cactus, two feet across, and I have been there for three winters. I have a nest of dry leaves and a roost of soft branches. The hollow is dry and warm. I am not inside it all the time. I go out to hunt.

My home is the hollow in the old cactus. I have been here for years. The ivy is thick, and the leaves are soft. I sleep in the deepest part, where the wind does not reach. I have a nest of twigs and feathers. I am warm here. The night is quiet.

I have a hollow in the cactus at the edge of the wood. The wood is a hundred yards wide, with a stream through it, and the lane comes up to it. The cactus is old and bent, with a hollow on the left side. I roost there, and I call from there.

My home is a hollow in an old cactus. It is in the hollow of a cactus, high in the ash, and I have lived there since I was a young owl. The cactus is old and gnarled, and the hollow is deep and dark. My home is a hollow in the old cactus at the edge of the wood. I have been there all my life. The wood is on the hill behind the barn, and the barn is where the lane goes past the stream. The stream is where the meadow ends. I am in the hollow, looking out through the leaves.
My home is a hollow in the old cactus at the edge of the wood. It is dark and dry and warm in winter, and the wind comes through the branches. I have been here for years. The wood is all I know.
